# Dror Kosowsky-Sachs

> Mechanical engineering and robotics student at the University of Maryland, graduating in Spring 2027. Builds robots end to end — mechanical design (SolidWorks), machining and fabrication (CNC milling, waterjet, lathe, 3D printing, laser cutting), electronics (KiCad PCB design, soldering, Arduino, Raspberry Pi), and robot software (ROS 2, Python, LiDAR-based navigation).

Every page is static HTML; all project text is in the page source.

Contact: drorks@terpmail.umd.edu · LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dror-kosowsky-sachs/

## Projects

- [Fish-Inspired UUV](https://droriks.github.io/uuv.html): Undergraduate research (May 2026 – present) in the UMD Hydrodynamics Lab, advised by Professor Cecilia Huertas-Cerdeira (ASPIRE Scholarship; presented at UMD's Summer Undergraduate Research Conference). Untethered fish-inspired UUV whose caudal fin is driven by a 4-DOF parallel manipulator (3RRS platform plus a roll servo): 50° sweep cone and 180° roll. Machined aluminum, multi-layer waterproofing, custom KiCad power PCB (11.1 V LiPo to 5 V and 7.4 V rails), and a ROS 2 pipeline on a Raspberry Pi (gait generator, numerical inverse kinematics, servo driver).
- [Autonomous Chess Board](https://droriks.github.io/chess-board.html): In progress. Raspberry Pi and computer vision chess board that moves its own pieces with magnets dragged by an H-bot gantry beneath the board; designed in SolidWorks, built with 3D printing and laser cutting.
- [Autonomous Maze Navigation](https://droriks.github.io/maze-navigation.html): ENAE450 Robotics Programming team project (Spring 2026). TurtleBot 4 maze escape using SLAM, AMCL, and Nav2 for the mapped race, and a ROS 2 Python LiDAR right-hand wall follower with geometric heading estimation and a state machine for the unmapped race.
- [Biometric Bike Lock](https://droriks.github.io/bike-lock.html): Arduino Uno bike lock that unlocks only with the correct fingerprint and paired key fob; DC motor and worm gear drive a locking pin through the spokes; Bluetooth status reporting; 3D-printed housing.
- [Robotic Fish: Flipper Propulsion](https://droriks.github.io/robotic-fish.html): Built in the UMD Hydrodynamics Lab to test flipper-based propulsion, with a force-measurement mount and a layer-jamming (vacuum-stiffened) tail.
